We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We must produce JSON tree: root molecule, then reaction node with template_id, children are precursor molecules (type mol). Then each precursor may be further broken down with next reaction etc.

We need to apply templates sequentially to break down target to precursors. The earlier attempts applied template 29646 to target and got three possible outcomes (three product sets). Need to choose one that can be further processed by next template 1914389, etc.

We need to construct a chain of 5 steps, each using given template id in order.

Thus step1: apply 29646 to target -> get some precursor(s). Choose one that matches template 1914389.

From result of 29646 we saw three possible outcomes (tuples). Let's parse them:

Result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O',))"

So three possible products (each a tuple of one SMILES). The third one looks like the original target? Actually third is "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O". That's similar but missing some groups? Not sure.

First product: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" includes a silyl protecting group.

Second product: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" includes silyl on acid.

We need to apply template 1914389 next. We attempted applying 1914389 to first product and got result: two precursors: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". So that seems good: it splits into a core and a side chain (maybe a protecting group). So step2 yields two precursors.

Now step3 must use template 1914390 on each of those? The order says after 1914389, we apply 1914390. Likely to one of the precursors (maybe the side chain). We attempted applying 1914390 to "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC" but got no result. However applying 1914390 to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" gave a product: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". That's a different molecule.

But we need to follow order: after step2 we have two precursors; we need to apply 1914390 to each? Or maybe to one of them to further break down. The template may apply to the core to give further precursors.

Let's apply 1914390 to the core "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". Already did, got one product (a new molecule). That product maybe can be further broken by 149040.

Now step4 template 149040. Apply to the product from step3? Let's try.
